done_when: A review that gets a 429 rate-limit answer waits and tries again before it counts as failed, so closes that start together all finish their reviews

known.title: A 429 usage-limit answer can still exhaust both review attempts
A rate-limited sign-off can repeatedly restart every review part
Follow-up: Exercise rate-limit retries through the Windows review wrapper

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - several reviews exhaust a shared Codex usage window and receive a 429. Codex maps a `usage_limit_reached` response to a message such as “You’ve hit your usage limit” ([mapping](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/codex-api/src/api_bridge.rs), [message](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/protocol/src/error.rs)). That message matches none of these patterns. `src/forge/autoreview.py:60` and `src/forge/autoreview.py:100` pass only the last nonempty output line as the reason, so when the helper returns that wording, close counts each response as a failure and stops after two attempts without waiting. The test supplies literal `429` strings instead. This misses the Done-when: “A review that gets a 429 rate-limit answer waits and tries again before it counts as failed, so closes that start together all finish their reviews”.
findings.title: A 429 usage-limit answer can still exhaust both review attempts

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - a client sign-off has 13 review parts and the service permits fewer simultaneous requests. `src/forge/review_process.py:69` launches every part concurrently, and a failed part fails the whole attempt. This new loop retries the entire sign-off after a recognized 429, launching all 13 parts together again; the same concurrency limit can therefore reject a part on every retry. Sign-off never completes and repeatedly runs the parts that already succeeded. `tests/test_signoff_checks_overlap.py:38` shows a 13-part product review.
Adds work: retry only failed sign-off parts; F 2 x H 2 = 4; 2 x C = 4
findings.title: A rate-limited sign-off can repeatedly restart every review part

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - concurrent closes encounter temporary throttling. The named proof runs one close, so it does not establish that closes started together all finish. It also replaces `review.time.sleep` with an immediate log write and checks the wait log separately from the review-call log. An implementation that retried immediately and performed the recorded sleeps only after the attempts would still pass, although it gives the service no time to recover. Exercise the concurrent commands and verify that each retry waits before the next attempt. The shim also depends on the private `review.time` import shape, so a behavior-preserving clock refactor breaks the test.
findings.title: Gate: test_1_close_waits_and_retries_rate_limits_before_counting_failures

findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 1, Harm 1
Windows uses the separate `review_process.py` wrapper at `src/forge/review.py:973`, so a wrapper regression that loses a 429 diagnostic would leave Windows closes stopping after two attempts while the Linux proof passes. The proof list leaves platform proof to pull request CI, but `.github/workflows/forge.yml:49` runs Linux, and the Windows suite in `.github/workflows/forge-next.yml:75` runs on a schedule or manual dispatch and selects only `platform`-marked tests; this test has no such mark.
Adds work: exercise the Windows wrapper in the retry test; F 1 x H 2 = 2; 2 x C = 2
findings.title: Follow-up: Exercise rate-limit retries through the Windows review wrapper

why: Closes that start together send their reviews at once, the review service answers 429, and each close stops after two failures (#1102)
